title: Jaipur Makes National Geographic's Best of the World 2027 as the Pink City Turns 300
excerpt: National Geographic's unranked list of 25 places for 2027 singles out Jaipur in its tricentennial year — palaces, a 400,000-strong literature festival, and a living crafts tradition.
body:
• National Geographic has named Jaipur one of its 25 Best of the World destinations for 2027, in a list released on October 20 covering six continents.
  • The timing is the story: Jaipur, founded on November 18, 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, celebrates its 300th anniversary in 2027.
  • Nat Geo singles out the Jaipur Literature Festival — roughly 400,000 visitors a year, with its 20th edition running January 14-18, 2027 — alongside Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar.
  • For diaspora travellers, the festival week in mid-January is the obvious anchor for a 2027 India trip: winter weather, the tricentennial year, and one of the world's largest literary gatherings in a single visit.

Jaipur has been named one of the world's 25 best places to travel in 2027 by National Geographic, earning its place on the magazine's annual Best of the World list in the year the Pink City turns 300. The list, released on October 20, spans six continents and is unranked — but Jaipur's entry carries a hook few rivals can match: a milestone anniversary, a palace city built for it, and one of the largest literary festivals on the planet.

"A 300-year-old city of palaces hosts one of the world's largest literary festivals" is how National Geographic sums up its case. The city, the magazine notes, is "known for its sandstone architecture and rich tradition of Indian crafts" — and in 2027, it adds, Jaipur is celebrating.

Why 2027 Is Jaipur's Year

Jaipur was founded on November 18, 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, a ruler-astronomer who laid out a planned grid city three centuries ago. That founding gives 2027 a ready-made narrative the list's editors look for: National Geographic says its annual selection hunts for destinations where "new itineraries, cultural revivals, and milestone celebrations make now the time to explore."

The centrepiece of the anniversary year is the Jaipur Literature Festival, which National Geographic says draws roughly 400,000 people annually. Its 20th edition runs January 14 to 18, 2027, at Hotel Clarks Amer, with readings, keynotes and panels spanning science, politics and history — past speakers include Booker Prize winner Kiran Desai and Nobel laureate J.M. Coetzee — plus the Jaipur Music Stage's folk, fusion and world music and art installations by Indian artists.

"The core spirit behind 'Best of the World' is to provide people with fresh, exciting, new reasons to get out there and see the world."

— Nathan Lump, Editor-in-Chief, National Geographic

The Palaces Behind the Pick

The list entry reads like a checklist of Jaipur's heavyweights. Amber Fort and Jaigarh Fort sit on adjacent hills on the city's northeast edge, their architecture mixing Rajput, Mughal and European influences, with Amber's interiors picked out for delicate floral inlay and carved marble panels. Hawa Mahal's honeycomb facade and latticed windows provide natural ventilation — the feature behind its name, "palace of the winds." Jantar Mantar, the 18th-century observatory built by the city's founder and now a UNESCO World Heritage site, holds the world's largest stone sundial. Jaipur itself was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2019.

The crafts economy gets equal billing. National Geographic points readers to Johari Bazaar and Chandpole Bazaar for everything from handmade shoes to gold kundan jewellery, to boutiques such as Anokhi and the PDKF Store for hand-block printing, and to the Museum of Meenakari Heritage, which documents the art of fusing powdered mineral glass onto gold. The dabu technique — hand-carved blocks stamping mud-resist paste onto cloth — is the kind of living craft tradition the list rewards.

Good Company on the List

Jaipur is the only Indian destination among the 25, which include Luxor ahead of the August 2, 2027 total solar eclipse, Normandy marking 1,000 years since the birth of William the Conqueror, Grenada's 150th Spicemas carnival, and Penang in Malaysia. A 26th spot, the Readers' Choice, went to Santa Catalina Island off California. Editor-in-chief Nathan Lump told USA Today the list is drawn from hundreds of nominations across National Geographic's community of writers, photographers and explorers, vetted for what he called a "wow factor" — and, increasingly, for alternatives to overtouristed standbys.

What It Means for a 2027 Trip

For Indian Americans and NRIs planning a 2027 India trip, the practical play is simple: build it around mid-January. The literature festival's January 14-18 window falls in Jaipur's best weather of the year — the October-to-March season — and the tricentennial guarantees a year of special programming beyond it. Travellers can read the full list and Nat Geo's Jaipur entry on the Best of the World 2027 page, and compare the coverage in CNN Travel's rundown of all 25 destinations. Three hundred years in, the Pink City has rarely had a better-timed invitation.
